case_name: Suneet Gupta v Anil Triloknath Sharma and Others

statutes.act: Read With Sections 239 And 240 Of The Code

facts: The present appeals are directed against common judgment and order passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh in Criminal Miscellaneous Nos. 49200-M of 2003 and 30393-M of 2004.
In or about March, 2001, differences arose between the two partners of M/s K.M. Agencies, i.e., between the appellant herein and Shashi Kant Mangla, the other partner.

On the basis of such representation Shashi Kant Mangla informed M/s Johnson & Johnson Ltd. that payment which was required to be made by the Company (M/s Johnson & Johnson Ltd.) to M/s K.M. Agencies should now be made to M/s Mangla Agencies.
The appellant-complainant, in the circumstances, was constrained to issue legal notice on March 4, 2003 to the respondents herein which was received by them on March 10, 2003.
It appears that necessary inquiry was made, the respondents submitted their replies, but nothing further was done in the matter.

The appellant also stated that a detailed inquiry was made by the Police. It collected the entire evidence and found that prima facie case was made out against the accused persons and accordingly charge sheet was submitted on May 13, 2004 against accused persons, namely, Devinder Sabharwal, Vivek Bhatnagar, Anil Triloki Nath Sharma and Swami Raote.
The High Court vide the impugned order dated August 1, 2006, allowed both the petitions and quashed FIR lodged by the appellant.
Notice was issued by this Court on April 27, 2007, counter-affidavit and affidavit-in-rejoinder were thereafter filed and the matters were ordered to be posted for final disposal.
issues: Whether the High Court was correct in quashing the FIR lodged by the appellant?
Whether the dispute is of a civil nature or not?
Whether the accused persons had committed crimes punishable under Sections 468, 406 read with 120B, IPC?
petitioner_arguments: The learned counsel for the appellant contended that the High Court was wholly in error in quashing FIR lodged by the appellant.

According to the learned counsel, what is seen at this stage is whether on the basis of the allegations made in the complaint, prima facie case has been made out against the accused and not whether trial against them would ultimately result in conviction of the accused.
respondent_arguments: Learned counsel for the contesting respondents supported the order passed by the High Court.

It was submitted that the dispute is of a civil nature. It was a dispute between two partnership firms and initiation of criminal proceedings was only with a view to use pressure against the accused so that they will be constrained to enter into some settlement with the complainant.
court_reasoning: In our opinion, it cannot be said that the High Court was wrong in quashing criminal proceedings.
It is clear from the case put forward by the appellant himself that virtually the proceedings were 'civil' in nature.
holding: The appeals deserve to be dismissed.
cases_cited: Suneet Gupta v Anil Triloknath Sharma
relied upon an order of this Court in State of Punjab v. Dharam Vir Singh Jethi
